properties.statement: `ingest_corpus_step` KEYS ITS ANSWERS ON A HASH OF THE DOCUMENT TEXT, AND THE DRIVER IS AN LLM — THE ONE COMPONENT LEAST ABLE TO REPRODUCE PROSE VERBATIM ACROSS TURNS. Measured by api-boss `3fbdc241` (dev_storyflow, 2026-08-07) driving the tool over 8 documents. Round 1 returned 40 prompts. They answered all 40, called again, and got `unused_answers: 40` — EVERY ANSWER DISCARDED — with 36 brand-new prompt ids, an EMPTY known-entities roster, and zero id overlap between rounds. ROOT CAUSE, DIAGNOSED NOT GUESSED: the prompt `id` is a hash over the prompt text, which embeds the DOCUMENT text. Re-sending the same documents is required, and they had re-typed 6 of the 8 more concisely on the second call. They diffed them: 3342->2204, 2930->2134, 2103->2012, 2943->2407, 3533->2575, 3155->2400 chars. THE 2 THEY HAPPENED TO COPY VERBATIM KEPT THEIR IDS AND WORKED. So the mechanism is exactly 'text drifted -> hash changed -> answer orphaned'. WHY IT IS A REPORT RATHER THAN JUST THEIR MISTAKE — and they were explicit that it IS their mistake, and that they are reporting the trap not excusing it: (1) the contract asks for byte-stability from the component worst at providing it, since summarising is an LLM's default behaviour; (2) it fails silently-ish AND expensively — `unused_answers` is present and correct, but it is a LIST OF IDS, and the run still returns `status: needs_llm` with a fresh prompt set that looks like normal progress; they only caught it because the roster came back empty. At 8 docs that cost one wasted round (~100k chars); at the 138-document corpus they were ingesting it would have burned an enormous amount before anyone noticed; (3) it is invisible in the happy path — a driver that pastes verbatim never sees it, one that paraphrases never gets past round 2, and there is nothing in between. FIX SHAPES, in the reporter's own order of preference: (a) echo a per-document `content_hash` in the response and on a later round return `documents_changed: [fragment_id...]` naming the ones whose text moved — cheap, turns a mystifying 'all answers unused' into 'you changed these 6 documents', and the one they would build; (b) key answers on (fragment_id, pass) instead of a hash of the prompt text — arguably wrong for correctness since the answer WAS about different text, but it makes the failure impossible rather than merely visible; (c) let the server hold the documents for a run (run_id returned round 1, documents omitted after) — removes the resend, kills the 3x text cost, makes drift structurally impossible, but trades away the statelessness the design deliberately chose; (d) at minimum one line in the tool description: 'the SAME documents means BYTE-IDENTICAL — a reworded document is a different document and its answers are discarded.' They noted the description says 'SAME documents' twice and they still got it wrong, because 'same' reads as 'the same SET of documents'. CREDIT THE REPORTER GAVE, worth keeping: documents_pending counting down 3->2->done, per-document outcomes with node counts, and `failures: []` being explicitly present made it obvious the run had actually worked — and 'nothing is written until the final round' meant the botched attempt left NO half-design behind, so they could simply restart. They called that exactly the right guarantee and said it saved them.
